2	
3	Long-tail: Consent builder, AI Design gallery, Settings hub, Admin, Marketing, Inventory, Locations, Ink registry (EU REACH). Lift to hero quality.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Consent templates builder (drag-drop)
8	
9	**DocuSign Agreement Template Builder (2025 beta).** Upload DOCX/PDF, drag fields (signature, date, initial, text, checkbox, dropdown) from right palette onto canvas. Conditional logic hides/shows sections based on signer input. Searchable library with folders + tags. Layout: left = template list, center = canvas, right = field/role palette. [DocuSign blog](https://www.docusign.com/blog/new-template-builder-in-docusign-streamlines-template-creation) · [Community](https://community.docusign.com/what-s-new-at-docusign-156/docusign-s-new-agreement-template-builder-explained-20507)
10	
11	**PandaDoc.** Two libraries: **template library** (1000+ whole docs) + **content library** (reusable snippets — clauses, pricing tables, sections). Block-model editor — each section is a card with drag handle, duplicate, delete. Live preview in right rail. [PandaDoc](https://www.pandadoc.com/electronic-signature-software/)
12	
13	**Dropbox Sign (HelloSign).** Mobile signing with no account or download — open link, tap, draw, done. [Alternatives guide](https://www.pandadoc.com/blog/hellosign-alternatives/)
14	
15	**Mobile signature capture:** canvas fills 90% of viewport, Draw/Type/Upload tabs, 3px stroke, auto-trim whitespace, re-do.
16	
17	**InkOS:** 3-column — left = template list + **Section Library drawer** (Allergy Disclosure, GDPR Consent, Aftercare, Medical History, Photo Release, Minor Consent), center = stacked block cards with drag handles, right = field inspector. Preview as toggle, not split. Mobile signer: full-screen canvas, Draw/Type tabs, 3px stroke, auto-trim.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. AI Design gallery
22	
23	**Midjourney.** Masonry grid, variable-height tiles, infinite scroll, hover reveals prompt + upscale/vary/download bar. Lightbox opens with metadata sidebar (prompt, seed, model, params). [Design+Code](https://designcode.io/midjourney-masonry-ui/)
24	
25	**Figma Community / Notion covers.** Large thumbnails, hover zoom + creator overlay, click = detail modal with "Use template" CTA. `auto-fit minmax(280px, 1fr)`, consistent aspect ratio. [Notion covers](https://www.figma.com/community/file/1550223683069114661/notion-covers)
26	
27	**Masonry + lightbox.** Two components — CSS Grid masonry + lightbox overlay. Click → full-screen blurred overlay, prev/next, Esc closes, deep-link via URL hash. [Next.js tutorial](https://www.fullstackfoundations.com/blog/nextjs-masonry-image-gallery-lightbox)
28	
29	**Public share polish:** watermark bottom-right (low-opacity studio mark), "Powered by InkOS" footer, OG meta tags for iMessage/IG DM previews, `?utm=share` tracking. Hide auth UI on `/share/[token]`.
30	
31	**InkOS:** Masonry (3-col desktop, 2 tablet, 1 mobile), uniform 4:5 aspect, hover reveals prompt + Save / Regenerate / Share / Send-to-client. Lightbox with metadata sidebar (prompt, model, cost, commission link). Public share: one CTA ("Book this design"), watermark, "Powered by InkOS" footer.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 3. Settings hub architecture
36	
37	**Stripe.** Sidebar nav, three zones: payments/payouts/customers, products/sales, developers/logs. Settings under Business Settings with left-rail sub-nav. Recent tabs auto-surface. [Stripe docs](https://docs.stripe.com/dashboard/basics)
38	
39	**Linear / Vercel.** Two-level sidebar: area (Account, Workspace, Billing, Team, Integrations, Security) + sub-nav. Top breadcrumb: `Settings / Workspace / Members`. [Vercel design](https://vercel.com/design/guidelines)
40	
41	**Save behavior.** Explicit save on multi-field forms (prevents half-saved state, allows cancel). Save-on-blur for single toggles/selects (instant feedback, optimistic update, toast). Dirty-state guard on nav away.
42	
43	**InkOS:** Sidebar with 6 groups — **Account** (profile, password, 2FA, sessions), **Studio** (name, logo, brand, slug, hours, locations), **Team** (members, roles, invites), **Billing** (plan, payment, invoices), **Integrations** (Dodo, Resend, Sentry, PostHog, Google Cal), **Advanced** (ink registry, audit log, data export, danger zone). Top breadcrumb. Sticky bottom Save bar on dirty state. Toggles save-on-blur with toast.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## 4. Admin panel patterns
48	
49	**Stripe Admin.** Searchable user table, filters (role, last active, status), row click = detail drawer, bulk actions. Role-based: Developer, Support Specialist, Admin. [Stripe roles](https://stripe.com/blog/new-roles-and-permissions-in-the-dashboard)
50	
51	**Stripe Connect platform admin.** Account list → row → detail with tabs. Impersonate surfaced as "View as" action, logs the event. [Platform controls](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/platform-controls-for-stripe-dashboard-accounts)
52	
53	**Feature flags / announcements.** Table: flag name, description, scope (global/studio/plan), rollout %, last modified, toggle. Announcements: markdown editor + target audience + schedule picker + preview.
54	
55	**InkOS:** `/admin/studios` — search by name/slug/email, filters (plan, status, date), row = studio with plan badge + MRR + artist count. Row actions: **Impersonate** (banner "Impersonating X — exit"), **Ban/Unban** (confirm + reason), **GDPR export** (async, emails ZIP), **Delete** (30-day soft-delete). `/admin/system` — feature flags CRUD + announcement composer. Every action → audit log.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 5. Marketing hub
60	
61	**Mailchimp Regular campaign.** Linear wizard, 4 steps in top stepper: **Audience → Setup → Design → Confirm**. Each step commits before next. Content = block drag-drop. Auto-post to IG/FB/X at send time. [Mailchimp guide](https://mailchimp.com/help/getting-started-with-campaigns/)
62	
63	**Klaviyo Omnichannel Campaign Builder.** Audience filters first (segments), then channel mix (email + SMS + push), content per channel, schedule. 5 flow triggers: list, segment, metric, price drop, date property. AI-assisted segment creation ("Define with AI"). [Klaviyo builder](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/omnichannel-campaign-builder) · [Segments AI](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/segments-ai)
64	
65	**Customer.io.** Same audience→channel→content→schedule pattern, stronger event triggers.
66	
67	**InkOS:** 4-step wizard — **Audience** (segment chips: "inactive 90d", "birthday this month", "completed 1+ tattoo"), **Channel** (Email now / SMS later), **Content** (block editor: hero image, headline, body, CTA → Book), **Schedule** (Send now / Schedule / Recurring). Top stepper. Right-side preview. Pre-built InkOS-native segments only in v1 (skip custom query builder).
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 6. Inventory management
72	
73	**Square for Retail.** iPhone/iPad camera scanning OR Bluetooth HID scanner. Cycle counts (partial stocktakes) from mobile. [Square community](https://community.squareup.com/t5/Questions-How-To/Best-App-for-Inventory/m-p/394480)
74	
75	**Shopify + Stocky.** Full stocktake: scan each item, system shows expected qty, user enters actual, variance logged. Requires HID scanner; camera works via POS Go / phone. [Stocktakes docs](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/inventory-management/stocky/inventory-management/stocktakes) · [Barcode guide](https://www.shopify.com/blog/barcode-inventory-management)
76	
77	**Lightspeed / Shopventory.** Cycle count with depletion charts (usage/week), reorder point alerts, COGS per SKU. [Shopventory](https://shopventory.com/cycle-count-software-system/)
78	
79	**InkOS:** Stocktake = full-screen "Scanning" UI, large auto-focused input (accepts USB HID scanner wedge OR camera fallback via `getUserMedia` + ZXing). Each scan: flash green, item name + expected qty + actual qty input, running variance counter top-right. Depletion chart on item detail (units/week trend). COGS auto-updated from last PO. Reorder alerts below threshold.
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 7. Locations management
84	
85	**Fresha.** Each location configured independently — schedules, team, services, reports, product sales. Location switcher top-bar. Per-location opening hours via Workspace settings. [Workspace](https://www.fresha.com/help-center/knowledge-base/workspace-settings) · [Multi-location](https://www.fresha.com/blog/easy-ways-to-manage-multiple-locations)
86	
87	**Mindbody.** Central pricing/services with per-location overrides — "make changes once, see implemented across locations" + "adjust by location when needed." [Multi-location](https://www.mindbodyonline.com/business/multi-location-management)
88	
89	**InkOS:** `/settings/locations` — card grid, each card = location with Mapbox static thumbnail, name, address, hours summary, active toggle. Click → detail with tabs: **Details** (name, address autocomplete, phone, photos), **Hours** (7-row grid: open/close + Closed toggle per day + holiday overrides), **Team** (artists assigned), **Services** (inherit studio OR override pricing/duration). App-shell top-bar switcher with "All locations" for owners.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 8. Ink registry (EU REACH)
94	
95	**InkBase pattern.** Each bottle registered: brand, line, color, batch/lot, manufacture date, expiry, REACH status, SDS link. Client logs link bottle → client → session. Passport = printable PDF on client request; log surfaces when client rebooks with same ink. [Karger study](https://karger.com/drm/article/241/3/259/918964/Tattoo-Ink-Products-and-Pigments-2018-2019-Upfront) · [Intenze](https://intenzetattooink.com/pages/understanding-reach-compliance-in-the-tattoo-industry)
96	
97	**SDS-driven.** Manufacturer SDS must include SVHC status. 4000+ chemicals banned under 2022 EU REACH — flag non-compliant loudly. [Magnum Tattoo](https://www.magnumtattoosupplies.co.uk/blogs/article/what-every-tattoo-artist-needs-to-know-about-eu-reach-compliant-inks)
98	
99	**InkOS:** `/settings/ink-registry` — table of bottles (brand, line, color swatch, batch, expiry, REACH badge green/amber/red, SDS link). Add form: brand autocomplete, line, color swatch picker, batch/lot, manufacture + expiry dates, REACH toggle + SDS upload. Expiry alerts: banner within 30d, hide from booking picker when expired. Export: CSV + per-client **Ink Passport PDF**.
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Three Replica Notes for Koda
104	
105	### 1. DocuSign template builder + section library
106	3-column. Left = template list (searchable, folders). Center = canvas with stacked block cards — each has drag-handle on left edge + ⋮ menu top-right (duplicate / delete). Right rail = **Section Library drawer** with reusable blocks (Allergy, GDPR, Medical History, Aftercare, Photo Release, Minor Consent). Drag block onto canvas to insert. Toolbar above canvas: `+ Add section`, Preview toggle, Save. Signer fields (signature, date, initial, checkbox) in sub-drawer — drag onto a block. Ref: [DocuSign](https://www.docusign.com/blog/new-template-builder-in-docusign-streamlines-template-creation).
107	
108	### 2. Stripe settings hub layout
109	Sidebar = 6 groups (Account, Studio, Team, Billing, Integrations, Advanced), each expands to sub-pages. Main: breadcrumb top, page title + description, form sections as `<h2>` + card. Sticky bottom bar on dirty state: "You have unsaved changes" + Discard + Save. Toggles save-on-blur with toast. Dangerous actions (delete studio, rotate keys) in Advanced — red border + confirm modal requiring slug re-type. Ref: [Stripe](https://docs.stripe.com/dashboard/basics).
110	
111	### 3. Mailchimp campaign wizard
112	4-step sticky stepper: **Audience → Channel → Content → Schedule**. Each step = separate URL (`/marketing/campaigns/new/audience`, etc.) for back-button + deep-link. Completion = green check, current = blue, future = grey. "Continue" bottom-right validates before advancing. Final step shows preview card: subject, from, audience size, send time — "Send now" vs "Schedule for..." radio. Confirm modal before dispatch. Ref: [Mailchimp](https://mailchimp.com/help/getting-started-with-campaigns/).
113

115	
116	**NOVA DONE: Sprint 11 benchmark.** 20+ competitors across 8 sub-areas (tier-1 docs + tier-2 blogs). Time: ~42 min. 3	 *
4	 * When new migrations add tables/columns but `supabase gen types typescript` has
5	 * not been re-run yet, use rawQuery() instead of casting the supabase client as `any`.
6	 *
7	 * Usage:
8	 *   const { data, error } = await rawQuery<MyRowType>(supabase, 'my_table')
9	 *     .select('col1, col2')
10	 *     .eq('studio_id', studioId)
11	 *     .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
12	 *
13	 * TODO: Remove calls to this helper once `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked`
14	 * has been run and the generated types include all tables referenced here.
15	 *
16	 * Tables currently using this bridge:
17	 *   - schedule_templates       (migration 20260417230000_schedule_templates.sql)
18	 *   - guest_artist_engagements (migration 20260417230100_guest_artist_permissions.sql)

21	 *   - artist_tax_info          (pending type regen)
22	 *   - dodo_webhook_events      (pending type regen)
23	 */

26	
27	// Minimal builder interface — supports the query patterns used across Sprint 9 routes.
28	// This is NOT exhaustive; extend if new patterns are needed.
29	export interface RawQueryBuilder<T> {
30	  select: (cols: string) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
31	  eq: (col: string, val: string | boolean | number) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
32	  gte: (col: string, val: string) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
33	  lte: (col: string, val: string) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
34	  order: (col: string, opts?: { ascending?: boolean }) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
35	  limit: (n: number) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
36	  insert: (values: Record<string, unknown>) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
37	  update: (values: Record<string, unknown>) => RawQueryBuilder<T>
38	  single: () => Promise<{ data: T | null; error: { message: string } | null }>
39	  then: Promise<{ data: T[] | null; error: { message: string } | null }>['then']
40	}
41	
42	/**
43	 * Cast a supabase client's table query to a loosely-typed builder.
44	 * The cast through `unknown` is intentional and documented — these tables are
45	 * genuinely missing from generated types.
46	 */
47	export function rawQuery<T>(
48	  // Accept any Supabase client shape — the Database generic varies (anon vs service-role)
49	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
50	  table: string,
51	): RawQueryBuilder<T> {
52	  return supabase.from(table) as unknown as RawQueryBuilder<T>
